## Part 0: Setting the workenvironment and loading the environment

```{r Installing packages, include = FALSE}
install.packages(c("stm", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "tidytext", "tidyr", "tidyverse", "data.table", "haven", "readxl", "quanteda", "text2map", "quanteda.textplots", "quanteda.textstats", "text2vec", "fpc", "factoextra", "textmineR"))
# Installazione del pacchetto principale
install.packages("quanteda")

# Installazione del pacchetto specifico per le statistiche testuali (necessario per textstat_simil)
install.packages("quanteda.textstats")

# Installazione del pacchetto per le visualizzazioni (opzionale, per i wordcloud)
install.packages("quanteda.textplots")
```

## Part 1: Inspecting differences with Favara and Tomasi (2026) 

```{r Inspect items}
## Inspect stoplist
head(words) # Di Liberatore final stoplist which is compared with custom_stops_en
## compared with Favara and Tomasi (2026) stoplist (1190) this is 1184 words long
## excluding precariousness, our list was 6 words longer than the final Di Liberatore stoplist

## Inspect vocabulary
head(vocab) # Di Liberatore final vocabulary, which is compared with vocab(tf)
## Compared with our vocabulary (1016), Di Liberatore is almost 200 words longer (861)
## this could be the effect of the final more restrictive stoplist (see above)

## Inspect documents list
head(ans_lis_filter) # Di liberatore final documents list, which is compared with our ans_list_filter
## Compared with out list (2476) which is 17 documents longer than Di Liberatore (2459)
## This difference ratio might result from a combination of stoplist - and lower.threshold choices (2) in stm::prepDocuments on the output of stm::textProcessor?


# **CONCLUSION**:
# it is the stoplist (words) the removes so many documents there is not any added lower.thresh = x
# See results from textpreprocessed in emotion article: 
# # Removing 720 of 1581 terms (720 of 16532 tokens) due to frequency 
# Removing 14 Documents with No Words 
# Your corpus now has 2459 documents, 861 terms and 15812 tokens.
```

```{r covariates in prevalence - precarity drivers dummy}
## Vulnerability normalised index (higher risk like in dummy subjective precarity)
meta |> 
  count(normepres) 
  
meta <- meta |>
  mutate(
    dum_normepres = if_else(normepres > 0.8, 1, 0)) 

meta |> 
  count(dum_normepres)

## Job Insecurity (higher gravity vs all)
meta |> 
  count(jobinsec)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(dum_jobinsec = if_else(jobinsec %in% c(1, 2), 1, 0))

meta |> 
  count(dum_jobinsec)

## Making ends meet (higher difficulty vs all) 
meta |> 
  count(endmeet)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(dum_endmeet = if_else(endmeet %in% c(1, 2), 1, 0))

meta |> 
  count(dum_endmeet)

## Capacity to pay unexpected expenses ("alone" vs all)
meta |> 
  count(unexpmix)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(dum_unexpmix = if_else(unexpmix %in% c(1), 1, 0))

meta |> 
  count(dum_unexpmix)

## Economic indipendence, it does not need any dummy recode
meta |> 
  count(ecoind)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(dum_ecoind = if_else(ecoind %in% c(1), 1, 0))

meta |> 
  count(dum_ecoind)

## Transform each variable in a factor (if not the estimate effect count it as numeric continous variable)
meta <- meta |>
  mutate(
    dum_normepres = factor(dum_normepres, levels = c(0,1)),
    dum_jobinsec  = factor(dum_jobinsec,  levels = c(0,1)),
    dum_endmeet   = factor(dum_endmeet,   levels = c(0,1)),
    dum_unexpmix  = factor(dum_unexpmix,  levels = c(0,1)),
    dum_ecoind    = factor(dum_ecoind,    levels = c(0,1))
  )

```

```{r covariates in prevalence - sociodemographic dummy}
## Gender; it does not need any recode 
meta |> 
  count(gender)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(dum_gender = if_else(gender %in% c(1), 1, 0))

meta |> 
  count(dum_gender)

## Age class (threshold below vs above 30 years old)
meta |> 
  count(ageyear)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(age_dum = ifelse(ageyear >=30, 1, 0)
         )

meta |> 
  count(age_dum)

## Migration background (autoctonous vs migrant)
meta |> 
  count(migrant)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(migr_dum = ifelse(migrant == 3, 1, 0)
         )

meta |> 
  count(migr_dum)

## Transformation in factor, as above
meta <- meta |>
  mutate(
    dum_gender = factor(dum_gender, levels = c(0, 1)),
    age_dum    = factor(age_dum,    levels = c(0, 1)),
    migr_dum   = factor(migr_dum,   levels = c(0, 1))
  )
```

```{r Likert scale of precarity - dummy and normalised index}
## Scale of subjectively perceived precarity - dummy
meta |> 
  count(prec)

meta <- meta |> 
  mutate(dum_prec = ifelse(prec >= 8, 1, 0)
         )
meta |> 
  count(dum_prec)

## Transfrom into a factor
meta <- meta |>
  mutate(
    dum_prec = factor(dum_prec, levels = c(0, 1))
  )

## Scale of subjectively perceived precarity - normalised index
meta <- meta |>
  mutate(
    normprec = (prec - min(prec, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                (max(prec, na.rm = TRUE) - min(prec, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

meta |> 
  count(normprec)
```

## Part 2: Re-estimating the models (with covariates in prevalence)

```{r Nested Model with Covariates in Prevalence 20k - sociodemographic characteristics}
# Covariate - basic model with included gender distinction
model_7 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ dum_gender,  
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)
saveRDS(model_7, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_7_stm_20_gender_DiLiberatore.rds")

# Covariate - basic model with included age distinction
model_8 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ age_dum,  
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)
saveRDS(model_8, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_8_stm_20_age_DiLiberatore.rds")

# Covariate - basic model with included migration background distinction
model_9 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ migr_dum,  
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)
saveRDS(model_9, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_9_stm_20_migration_DiLiberatore.rds")
```

```{r Nested Model with Covariates in Prevalence 20k - precarity drivers}
# Covariate - normalised vulnerability index from Epres-scale
model_2 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ dum_normepres,  
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)

saveRDS(model_2, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_2_stm_20k_vuln_DiLiberatore.rds")

# Covariate - included perceived job insecurity
model_3 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec,  
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)

saveRDS(model_3, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_3_stm_20k_vuln_jobinsec_DiLiberatore.rds")

# Covariate - included difficulty in making ends meet
model_4 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec + dum_endmeet,  
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)

saveRDS(model_4, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_4_stm_20k_vuln_jobinsec_endmeet_DiLiberatore.rds")

# Covariate - included capacity to individually pay unexpecte expenses
model_5 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec + dum_endmeet + dum_unexpmix,
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)

saveRDS(model_5, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_5_stm_20k_vuln_jobinsec_endmeet_unexpmix_DiLiberatore.rds")

# Covariate - included feeling to be economic of indipendence from family of origin
model_6 <- stm(documents = docs,
               vocab = vocab, 
               K = 20,
               prevalence = ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec + dum_endmeet + dum_unexpmix + dum_ecoind,  
               data = meta,
               verbose = FALSE,seed=2024)

saveRDS(model_6, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/model_6_stm_20k_vuln_jobinsec_endmeet_unexpmix_ecoind_DiLiberatore.rds")
```

```{r Documents associated with topics - with base model}
## Save Di Liberatore filtered list of documents (size = 2459 docs)
saveRDS(ans_lis_filter, file = "C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/ans_lis_filter.rds")
# Load filtered documents (in character, not as numbered documents)
ans_lis_filter <- readRDS("C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Models/DiLiberatore/ans_lis_filter.rds")

# open a loop
K <- model_1$settings$dim$K  # total number of topics in the STM
# save results in pdf
pdf("C:/Users/vicio/Desktop/Rev_STM/Results/DiLiberatoreResults/STM_Topic_Quotes_DiLiberatore.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)

for (k in 1:K) {
  # findThoughts returns a list $docs, where each element corresponds to one topic
  # Here we extract the first (and only) element for the current topic k
  thoughts <- findThoughts(model_1,
                           texts = ans_lis_filter,
                           n = 2,      # number of representative phrases per topic
                           topics = k)$docs[[1]]
  
  # Plot the representative phrases for the current topic
  plotQuote(thoughts,
            main = paste("Topic", k),
            width = 80,     # maximum line width for each phrase
            text.cex = 0.8) # font size for the text
}
#close pdf
dev.off()
```

## Part 4: Studying estimated effect of included covariates

```{r Estimate effect of nested prevalenced-based covariate model}
K <- model_1$settings$dim$K 
for (k in 1:K) {
effects_2 <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ dum_normepres,  
                          stmobj = model_2,
                          metadata = meta, 
                          uncertainty = "Global")

effects_3 <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec,  
                          stmobj = model_3,
                          metadata = meta, 
                          uncertainty = "Global")

effects_4 <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec + dum_endmeet,  
                          stmobj = model_4,
                          metadata = meta, 
                          uncertainty = "Global")

effects_5 <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec + dum_endmeet + dum_unexpmix,  
                          stmobj = model_5,
                          metadata = meta, 
                          uncertainty = "Global")

effects_6 <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec + dum_endmeet + dum_unexpmix + dum_ecoind,  
                          stmobj = model_6,
                          metadata = meta, 
                          uncertainty = "Global")

effects_7 <- estimateEffect(1:K ~ dum_gender,  
                          stmobj = model_7,
                          metadata = meta,
```

```{r Analysis 1: Semantic Stability Check (Side-by-Side Table)}

library(stm)
library(tidyverse)
library(writexl)

# --- 1. Extract Top Words from Model 0 (Base) ---
labels_0 <- labelTopics(model_0, n = 5)
# FIX: Do NOT use t() here. The matrix is already 20 rows x 5 columns.
topics_0 <- data.frame(labels_0$prob) 
colnames(topics_0) <- paste0("Base_Word_", 1:5)
topics_0$Topic <- 1:20  # Now this will match (20 rows)

# --- 2. Extract Top Words from Model Tomasi (Covariates) ---
labels_t <- labelTopics(model_tomasi, n = 5)
# FIX: Do NOT use t() here either.
topics_t <- data.frame(labels_t$prob)
colnames(topics_t) <- paste0("Tomasi_Word_", 1:5)
topics_t$Topic <- 1:20

# --- 3. Merge and Compare ---
comparison_table <- left_join(topics_0, topics_t, by = "Topic") |>
  select(Topic, Base_Word_1, Tomasi_Word_1, Base_Word_2, Tomasi_Word_2, Base_Word_3, Tomasi_Word_3)

# --- 4. View and Save ---
print(comparison_table)
write_xlsx(comparison_table, "Emo_Results/Model_Comparison_TopWords.xlsx")
```

```{r Analysis 2: Semantic Coherence vs. Exclusivity (The Pareto Plot)}

# --- CALCULATE METRICS ---
# Ensure you have the 'docs' object loaded from your pre-processing environment!
# If your object is named 'emo_docs' or 'out$documents', replace 'docs' below.

# 1. Base Model Metrics
sem_0 <- semanticCoherence(model_0, documents = docs, M = 10)
exc_0 <- exclusivity(model_0)

# 2. Your Model Metrics
sem_t <- semanticCoherence(model_tomasi, documents = docs, M = 10)
exc_t <- exclusivity(model_tomasi)

# --- PLOTTING ---
png("Emo_Results/Coherence_Exclusivity_Comparison.png", width = 8, height = 6, units = "in", res = 300)

# Create empty plot frame
plot(sem_0, exc_0, 
     xlim = c(min(sem_0, sem_t) - 5, max(sem_0, sem_t) + 5), 
     ylim = c(min(exc_0, exc_t) - 0.5, max(exc_0, exc_t) + 0.5),
     xlab = "Semantic Coherence (Higher is Better)", 
     ylab = "Exclusivity (Higher is Better)",
     main = "Model Diagnostics: Base vs. Covariate Model",
     type = "n") # 'n' means don't plot points yet

# Add Base Model (Blue)
text(sem_0, exc_0, labels = 1:20, col = "blue", cex = 0.8)
points(mean(sem_0), mean(exc_0), col = "blue", pch = 19, cex = 1.5) # Centroid

# Add Tomasi Model (Red)
text(sem_t, exc_t, labels = 1:20, col = "red", cex = 0.8)
points(mean(sem_t), mean(exc_t), col = "red", pch = 19, cex = 1.5) # Centroid

# Add Legend and Arrows
legend("bottomleft", legend = c("Base Model (Di Liberatore)", "Covariate Model (Tomasi)"),
       col = c("blue", "red"), pch = 1, lty = 1)

dev.off()

```

```{r Analysis 3: Explanatory Power (Held-Out Likelihood)}

# 1. Create a Held-Out Set (10% of data hidden)
# 'out$documents' and 'out$vocab' come from your textProcessor output
heldout <- make.heldout(out$documents, out$vocab, N = floor(0.1 * length(out$documents)))

# 2. Run Base Model on Training Set (No Covariates)
# Note: We use lower iterations just for the test comparison
model_base_held <- stm(documents = heldout$documents, vocab = heldout$vocab, 
                       K = 20, prevalence = NULL, # NO COVARIATES
                       data = meta, max.em.its = 50, verbose = FALSE, seed = 2024)

# 3. Run Your Model on Training Set (With Covariates)
model_tomasi_held <- stm(documents = heldout$documents, vocab = heldout$vocab, 
                         K = 20, 
                         # INSERT YOUR EXACT FORMULA HERE:
                         prevalence = ~ dum_normepres + dum_jobinsec + dum_endmeet + dum_unexpmix, 
                         data = meta, max.em.its = 50, verbose = FALSE, seed = 2024)

# 4. Calculate Likelihood on the Hidden (Held-out) Data
eval_base   <- eval.heldout(model_base_held, heldout$missing)
eval_tomasi <- eval.heldout(model_tomasi_held, heldout$missing)

# 5. Print Results
cat("Held-Out Likelihood (Higher is Better):\n")
cat("Base Model:", eval_base$expected.heldout, "\n")
cat("Your Model:", eval_tomasi$expected.heldout, "\n")

# If eval_tomasi$expected.heldout is HIGHER (less negative) than Base,
# you have statistically proven your model is superior.

```

```{cosine similarity and tf_idf}
library(stm)
library(quanteda)
library(quanteda.textstats)
library(Matrix)
df <- read_xlsx("~/Desktop/Tesi/file_r/data/df_complete_3.xlsx")
processed <- textProcessor(
  documents = df$text, 
  metadata = df,
  language = "english",
  stem = TRUE,
  removestopwords = TRUE,
  customstopwords = words,
  custompunctuation = c("-"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

out <- prepDocuments(
  documents = processed$documents, 
  vocab = processed$vocab, 
  meta = processed$meta
)

row_indices <- rep(1:length(out$documents), sapply(out$documents, ncol))
col_indices <- unlist(lapply(out$documents, function(x) x[1, ]))
counts <- unlist(lapply(out$documents, function(x) x[2, ]))

sparse_mat <- sparseMatrix(
  i = row_indices,
  j = col_indices,
  x = counts,
  dims = c(length(out$documents), length(out$vocab))
)

filtered_dtm <- as.dfm(sparse_mat)
colnames(filtered_dtm) <- out$vocab
docvars(filtered_dtm) <- out$meta

filtered_tfidf <- dfm_tfidf(filtered_dtm)

sim_matrix <- textstat_simil(filtered_dtm, method = "cosine")
sim_matrix_raw <- as.matrix(sim_matrix)
diag(sim_matrix_raw) <- NA
mean_cosine <- mean(sim_matrix_raw, na.rm = TRUE)

print(mean_cosine)
```
